outlook.statement: Aim to become India's largest and perhaps the world's most admired bullion enterprise by helping families preserve wealth through gradual gold accumulation via Aurel Gold/Silver Purchase Plans.

With a zero-debt balance sheet, growing branded plan subscriber base, a strengthened B2B dealer network, and the structural tailwind of record gold prices driving Indian physical investment demand, your Company is strongly positioned for sustained profitable growth in the years ahead.

Long-term fundamentals for physical bullion remain strongly supportive. The Company continues to explore prudent avenues to strengthen its financial base and accelerate scale, in full adherence with the applicable regulatory framework.
The physical bullion market in India is at an inflection point. The companies that build brand, compliance infrastructure, and distribution in this window will own the category for the next decade.
Priority for FY 2026-27 is to translate substantial revenue scale-up into improved PAT margins through higher mix of branded plan revenue (GPP/SPP), B2B programme fees, and export-linked transactions

risks: Inventory valuation adjustments under Ind AS 2 due to precious metal price corrections
Gold price volatility making bullion less affordable for Indian households
Net Realisable Value (NRV) adjustment impact on inventories due to precious metal price volatility
Transient accounting impact from inventory markdown under Ind AS 2

Capital Intensity and Price-Level Risk: The Company operates with a modest capital base in a scale-driven, price-sensitive industry. With gold above ₹1,50,000/10g and silver above ₹2,50,000/kg, the value of inventory holdings, working capital requirements, and hedging margins have surged significantly. Achieving Qualified Jeweller (QJ) status on the IIBX, which requires approximately ₹15 crore net worth, remains a medium-term aspiration that constrains access to exchange-based sourcing advantages.

Geopolitical and Macroeconomic Headwinds: The US-Israel-Iran conflict and ongoing US-China trade tensions introduce volatility in global commodity markets. These dynamics can compress margins, disrupt cross-border bullion flows, and complicate medium-term planning.

Revenue Concentration and Margin Compression: FY 2025–26 saw a substantial increase in total revenue driven by high-volume bullion and derivative trading. However, this growth was accompanied by margin compression, with PAT declining year-on-year. The Company is focused on improving the quality and consistency of margins through higher-value B2B programme revenue, branded plan enrolments, and export-linked business.

Evolving Customer Behaviour: A growing cohort of younger investors prefers digital-first gold exposure via ETFs, digital gold apps, and online platforms. While this is a structural headwind for purely physical demand, the Company believes its personalised, compliance-first model—combined with a digital asset portfolio—positions it effectively across both segments.

Macroeconomic Sensitivity: Consumer sentiment, inflation, currency movements, and broader economic stability directly affect offtake in both retail and B2B channels. A below-normal monsoon or any sustained inflationary shock from the Middle East conflict could curb buying capacity among retail customers.

key_audit_matters: NRV-based valuation of inventories (gold bullion, silver bullion, jewellery, and securities) under Ind AS 2

NRV Impact on Inventories: In compliance with Ind AS 2 - Inventories, the Company's gold bullion, silver bullion, jewellery, and securities are carried at the lower of cost or Net Realisable Value (NRV). FY 2025-26 was a year of unprecedented precious metal price volatility, with gold touching an all-time high of US$5,405/oz in January 2026 before experiencing a sharp correction. This trajectory created conditions where certain inventory positions, acquired at elevated cost levels prior to the correction, were required to be marked down to their NRV at 31st March, 2026. This mandatory non-cash accounting adjustment under Ind AS 2, while not representing any physical loss or diminution in the underlying commercial value of inventory, had a measurable impact on gross margins and consequently reported PAT for the year. The Statutory Auditors validated the appropriateness of this NRV-based valuation as a Key Audit Matter in their report for FY 2025-26.

Valuation of Inventories (Gold & Silver Bullion and Traded Securities) - Inventory aggregating Rs. 39,998.96 thousands valued at cost or NRV; procedures included testing inventory listing, assessing cost methodology (FIFO for securities, cost of purchase for bullion), comparing carrying values to MCX closing prices, evaluating NRV of securities via quoted prices, attending physical verification, evaluating disclosures per Ind AS 2

Revenue Recognition from Bullion, Jewellery and Derivative Transactions - Revenue Rs. 8,47,526.98 thousands; procedures included assessing revenue recognition policies per Ind AS 115, substantive testing of sales transactions, independent verification of derivative contract notes and broker statements, analytical procedures, cut-off testing, examining unusual transactions

Related Party Transactions - Significant transactions with related parties and KMP remuneration; procedures included obtaining related party list, testing sample transactions, comparing pricing with market transactions, reviewing Board approvals and compliance with Sections 177 and 188, assessing disclosures per Ind AS 24
